metaData.originalTitle: 就从来没人质疑过 OPD 的 reward 设计吗？我们发现了 log 本身就是问题，也许就不该用！
metaData.title: Has no one ever questioned OPD's reward design? We found that log itself is the problem—maybe it shouldn't be used!
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This paper diagnoses that the unbounded log-ratio reward in vanilla OPD causes training instability, and proposes PowerOPD, which replaces log with the Box-Cox power transformation, making the reward naturally bounded and sign-consistent. Experiments show it is more stable, stronger, and more resource-efficient.
metaData.summary: The article first points out that On-Policy Distillation (OPD) has become a standard component in post-training of large models, but mainstream sampled-token OPD (vanilla OPD) suffers from severe training pathologies: accuracy first drops then rises, response length oscillates, and final performance falls more than 8 points behind full-vocab OPD. By analyzing the reward distribution, the author identifies the root cause as the unbounded log-ratio reward (negative tail approaching -50), with extreme rewards concentrated in the early rollout stage and persisting throughout training. Comparing post-hoc fixes such as clip, tanh, and z-score, it is found that none can fundamentally solve the problem because log itself amplifies low-probability differences into extreme values. To address this, the author proposes PowerOPD: replacing log with the Box-Cox power transformation yields a family of bounded ([-1,1]) and sign-consistent rewards, and introduces a tunable parameter α as a "probability region selector" to filter low-probability noise. Experiments on multiple Qwen3 teacher-student settings and six mathematical reasoning benchmarks show that PowerOPD significantly outperforms vanilla OPD (average +4.47 Avg@8 / +4.06 Pass@8), surpasses all post-hoc methods, and even beats full-vocab OPD (up to +2.59 Avg@8 / +8.90 Pass@8), while saving 59.2% training time and 23.1% GPU memory. Gradient norm analysis reveals that PowerOPD gradients remain consistently in the 0.25-0.35 range, whereas vanilla OPD has an initial spike close to 1000 (a 3000x gap), demonstrating fundamental stability.

mainPoints.point: The log-ratio reward in vanilla OPD is unbounded, which is the root cause of training instability.
mainPoints.explanation: Log diverges as probability approaches 0, leading to extreme rewards (negative tail near -50) and high-variance gradients, and this problem persists throughout training and is not eliminated by warmup.

mainPoints.point: Post-hoc fixes such as clip, tanh, and z-score cannot fundamentally solve the problem.
mainPoints.explanation: These methods compress only after log has already magnified the values, which is too late; z-score can even flip the sign of the reward, causing incorrect learning direction and performing worse than no fix.

mainPoints.point: PowerOPD replaces log with the Box-Cox power transformation, making the reward naturally bounded and sign-consistent.
mainPoints.explanation: PowerOPD satisfies boundedness ([-1,1]) and sign consistency (positive when teacher probability is higher, negative when student is higher, zero when equal), eliminating the unbounded issue at the mapping level.

mainPoints.point: The parameter α acts as a 'probability region selector'; larger α focuses more on high-probability tokens, filtering low-probability noise.
mainPoints.explanation: α controls the degree to which reward magnitude is tied to absolute probability. Experiments show that larger α yields higher accuracy, shorter responses, and more stable training.

mainPoints.point: After replacing the unbounded log reward with a bounded power reward, sampled-token OPD becomes stronger, faster, and more resource-efficient than full-vocab OPD.
mainPoints.explanation: The bottleneck of sampled-token OPD is not the sampling itself, but the reward shaping.

keyQuotes: As long as log remains, the mapping from probability to reward is unbounded, and any subsequent remedial measures are just dealing with the consequences.
Vanilla OPD is not a completely different design; it is the unbounded limit of PowerOPD when α=1.
The problem isn't that the post-processing is insufficient—it's log itself. What really needs to change is the mapping function from probability to reward.

relatedArticles.title: Envisioning the Possible Future of Multimodal Understanding: From Describing the World to Entering the World
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explores the future evolution of multimodal understanding, arguing that it should progress from static, offline, question-answering capabilities to dynamic, online world-understanding systems with long-term memory and decision-making participation, and elaborates on six key trends: native multimodality, streaming video understanding, long-term memory, multimodal retrieval, serving as a judge for generative models, and spatial intelligence.

relatedArticles.title: DeepSeek-R1 and V3.2: Insights into Post-training and RL Training Stability
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the entire DeepSeek-R1 training process, covering the transition from R1-Zero's pure reinforcement learning exploration to R1's multi-stage alignment strategy, and explores the R3 routing mechanism as well as KL divergence and stability optimization in RL training.

relatedArticles.title: 140. A 4-Hour Interview with Yao Shunyu: Let Me Be a Little Crazy! Training Models at Anthropic and Gemini, Tech Predictions, and the End of Heroism
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: An in-depth conversation with former Anthropic and Google DeepMind researcher Yao Shunyu, sharing frontline experience training Claude 3.7/4.5 and Gemini 3, exploring that model capabilities have not plateaued, the arrival of the AI collectivism era, and the true driving forces behind technological development.

relatedArticles.title: Wang Jianshuo: Markdown is the New Programming Language
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Wang Jianshuo proposes that natural language is the new 'assembly language,' LLMs are the new compilers, and programmers should completely abandon directly modifying AI-generated code, instead writing repeatable engineering at the higher natural language layer.

relatedArticles.title: A Serious Discussion: How Much of Our Skills Can Skill Actually Distill? | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the capability boundaries of AI Agent Skills, pointing out that while they excel at encoding explicit rules and knowledge routing, they cannot capture the tacit intuition and utility judgment that human experts rely on in complex decision-making.

relatedArticles.title: Where Does Agentic Capability Come From? Deconstructing the Training Process of Foundation Models GLM-5 / MiniMax M2 / Kimi K2.5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth breakdown of the full training pipeline for modern Agentic LLMs, represented by GLM-5, detailing the complete methodology from foundation pre-training and multi-stage post-training (RL) to Agentic data synthesis.

relatedArticles.title: SGLang Overview: Design Philosophy and Key Mechanisms
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the SGLang inference engine's design philosophy, focusing on how it balances throughput and latency under memory constraints through Chunked Prefill, CPU/GPU overlap, and fine-grained memory management.

relatedArticles.title: Reverse Engineering and Systematic Analysis of Claude Code! Harness Engineering: A Complete Guide Based on Claude Code
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Through a deep reverse engineering of Claude Code's 500,000 lines of source code, this article systematically dissects the design philosophy, core architecture, and engineering implementation details of the AI Agent infrastructure known as 'Harness Engineering'.

relatedArticles.title: In-Depth Analysis of How Hermes Agent Achieves "Self-Evolution" and Its Design Practices for Prompt / Context / Harness
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core mechanism by which Hermes Agent achieves "self-evolution" through dynamic Skill generation and an RL training loop, and deconstructs its design practices from three engineering dimensions: Prompt, Context, and Harness.

relatedArticles.title: When Can Agents Write Their Own Skills? | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth review of the evolution of AI Agent skills—from manual refinement to autonomous discovery, encapsulation, and continuous evolution—and systematically outlines the core breakthroughs in Agent skill lifecycle management in academia and industry between 2025 and 2026.
